metadata.name: SCORE2 (Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2, Age 40–69)
metadata.summary: Estimates 10-year risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular disease in apparently healthy adults aged 40–69 years without diabetes, recalibrated to European risk regions.
clinical_pearls: Risk thresholds depend on age: <50 years (<2.5% low-to-moderate, 2.5–7.4% high, >=7.5% very high) vs 50–69 years (<5% low-to-moderate, 5–9.9% high, >=10% very high).
Do not use SCORE2 for patients with type 2 diabetes (use SCORE2-Diabetes) or established ASCVD (use SMART2), or adults >=70 years (use SCORE2-OP).
Incorporates competing non-CVD mortality risk and contemporary European incidence data to estimate combined fatal and nonfatal MI and stroke.

Pitfall — Geographic & uncaptured risk enhancers: Derived and calibrated for European populations (interpret cautiously outside Europe); does not include Lp(a), family history, CKD, or chronic inflammatory diseases.

options.label: Low-risk region (e.g., Western Europe, UK, Spain)
Very-high-risk region (e.g., Eastern Europe / Central Asia)

interpretation.label: Low-to-Moderate Risk (<2.5%, Age <50)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk <2.5% for adults under 50 years. Risk factor treatment generally not recommended unless specific modifiers apply.

interpretation.label: High Risk (2.5–7.4%, Age <50)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk 2.5% to <7.5% for adults under 50 years. Consider risk factor treatment alongside lifestyle optimization.

interpretation.label: Very High Risk (>=7.5%, Age <50)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk >=7.5% for adults under 50 years. Risk factor pharmacotherapy generally recommended.

interpretation.label: Low-to-Moderate Risk (<5%, Age 50–69)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk <5% for adults aged 50–69 years. Emphasize lifestyle measures.

interpretation.label: High Risk (5.0–9.9%, Age 50–69)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk 5% to <10% for adults aged 50–69 years. Consider BP and lipid-lowering therapy.

interpretation.label: Very High Risk (>=10%, Age 50–69)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk >=10% for adults aged 50–69 years. Risk factor pharmacotherapy generally recommended.

assessment_guides.title: Selecting ESC Cardiovascular Risk Region
bedside_steps: Match the patient's country of residence to the WHO/ESC 4-tier CVD mortality classification (Low, Moderate, High, Very high).
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Regional recalibration significantly shifts absolute 10-year risk estimates for identical clinical inputs.
